posts.text: My piece on the self-dealing of Trump during his second term has gotten a lot of traction, invited endless criticism and questions, and I thought I should respond to as much of it as possible. So, today, I published a follow-up piece answering those Qs and criticism.
Here is the full thing: readtangle.com/responses-to-…

Massive win for Rs, good outcome for democracy, bad outcome for Ds, and terrible outcome for Trump facing repercussions for his awful gerrymandering war.


Josh Gerstein (@joshgerstein)

FLASH: Virginia Supreme Court, 4-3, overturns redistricting referendum that could have netted Democrats 5 additional House seats. Doc:
vacourts.gov/static/opinions…

We are in deep, deep trouble. 

A reader wrote in to me this week saying that they wouldn't read my Trump corruption story because ChatGPT "fact-checked the piece" and informed them most of it was false.

Among other things, ChatGPT told them that there is no Iran war, Jared Kushner is not a negotiator in the war, Qatar never offered Trump a $400 million plane, George Santos wasn't pardoned, the NYTimes did not report on Syrian billionaires lobbying Trump for sanctions relief, Trump never launch
Here is my story, with links to each claim readtangle.com/the-everythin…

For those asking, 1) It was a free version of ChatGPT, but the reader then did it in a paid version and got nearly identical results, 2) The prompt was just to fact-check the piece, and 3) Chat figured it out once it saw an article link

The worst presidency for speech rights in the modern era. Not close.


Kyle Griffin (@kylegriffin1)

MS NOW Exclusive:

The FBI has launched a criminal leak investigation focusing on Atlantic magazine journalist Sarah Fitzpatrick, who wrote that deeply unflattering account of Kash Patel's work habits.

There is deep concern about this approach among some of the FBI agents. ms.now/news/fbi-investigatin…




— https://nitter.net/kylegriffin1/status/2052030643752649150#m

This is an encouraging development.


Annmarie Hordern (@annmarie)

ABC: The DOJ is investigating a series of suspiciously timed trades in the oil market just ahead of major announcements by Trump about the war against Iran, sources told ABC News. The DOJ, along with the CFTC, is probing at least four of these trades where traders made a total of more than $2.6 billion betting that oil prices would drop right before they did.
